steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
Here’s a quick rundown of the main differences between DNA and RNA:

1. Sugar backbone  
   • DNA contains deoxyribose (missing one oxygen atom)  
   • RNA contains ribose (has that extra –OH group)

2. Nitrogenous bases  
   • DNA uses adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C), guanine (G)  
   • RNA uses A, cytosine (C), guanine (G), and uracil (U) instead of thymine

3. Structure  
   • DNA is typically a double helix—two strands wound around each other  
   • RNA is usually single-stranded, though it can fold into complex shapes

4. Location and stability  
   • DNA resides mainly in the cell nucleus (and mitochondria), is more chemically stable  
   • RNA is found in nucleus and cytoplasm, is less stable (degrades more easily)

5. Primary functions  
   • DNA stores and transmits genetic information long-term  
   • RNA translates that code into proteins (mRNA), helps with protein synthesis (tRNA, rRNA), and has regulatory roles

In under a minute, that covers the core chemical and functional distinctions!
